test_title: PYST 37: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT correct for uniform velocity?

options.text: Velocity is constant and acceleration is zero.
The slope of the line in v-t graph is zero.
The v–t graph is a horizontal line.
The area under the v–t graph gives acceleration.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The area under the v-t graph gives acceleration.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Velocity is constant and acceleration is zero:** When an object moves with **uniform velocity**, its speed and direction remain constant. As there is no change in velocity, the **acceleration is zero**. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **The slope of the line in the v-t graph is zero:** In a velocity-time graph for uniform velocity, the slope represents acceleration. Since the velocity remains constant, the slope of the graph is zero. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **The v-t graph is a horizontal line:** For uniform velocity, the velocity does not change over time. Therefore, the velocity-time graph is a **horizontal line parallel to the time axis**. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **The area under the v-t graph gives acceleration:** The area under the velocity-time graph does not represent acceleration. Instead, it represents the **displacement** of the object. Acceleration is determined by the **slope** of the v-t graph. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Velocity:**

 
 
• When an object moves with uniform velocity, its speed and direction remain unchanged throughout its motion.
 
• The object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• In such cases, the acceleration is zero, as there is no change in velocity.
 
 
 
• **Velocity-Time Graph:**
 
 
• The slope of a velocity-time graph represents the acceleration of an object.
 
• A horizontal line on the graph indicates constant velocity (zero acceleration).
 
• If the graph is inclined upwards, it indicates positive acceleration; if inclined downwards, it indicates negative acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Area under the v-t Graph:**
 
 
• The area under the velocity-time graph is equal to the **displacement** of the object.
 
• For example, if a car travels at a constant velocity of 60 m/s for 10 seconds, the displacement is 60 times 10 = 600 {m} .
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, mathematically defined as a = (Delta v)/(Delta t) .
 
• In cases of uniform velocity, acceleration is zero as there is no change in velocity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Displacement vs Distance:** Displacement is a vector quantity that measures the shortest path between two points, whereas distance is a scalar quantity that measures the total path traveled.
 
• **Instantaneous vs Average Velocity:** Instantaneous velocity is the velocity of an object at a particular instant, while average velocity is calculated over a time interval.
 
• **Real-Life Example of Uniform Velocity:** A satellite orbiting Earth at a constant speed along a circular path exhibits uniform velocity if its direction does not change.
 
• **Graphical Representation:** The graphical interpretation of motion concepts such as velocity, acceleration, and displacement helps in visualizing the relationships between these quantities.
